new: except the basic nodes along a tile edge whose doorway is part of the route (see §6.5),
rationale: The number of traps must not depend on which tiles happen to touch; the exclusion is keyed to the doorways the party uses.

old: When they are in play, a *PvP encounter* follows the defeat of each boss, as in the standard game.
new: When they are in play, a *PvP encounter* follows the defeat of each boss whose defeat completes a section. A boss defeated before its section is completed is followed by no PvP encounter.
rationale: A contest in the middle of a section handed a co-operating party a full restoration; tying the contest to the end of a section removes that and the rule that restored characters to an earlier state.

old: When the boss's defeat completes a section, the setup and the rest that follow the PvP encounter are those of the completed section (see §18.1, Section Completion; §20.9). When the boss's defeat does not complete its section, no rest follows the PvP encounter. Every character who took part is instead restored as at the start of the PvP encounter (see §20.1), each character who died in it returns to the tile, and the exploration continues.
new: The setup and the rest that follow the PvP encounter are those of the completed section (see §18.1, Section Completion; §20.9).

old: An invader appears once. Whether it was killed or vanished,
new: An invader appears once, unless a campaign states otherwise (see §19.4; §19.15). Whether it was killed or vanished,
rationale: Two campaigns bring a listed invader back until it is killed; the general rule now points to them.

old: The number of characters is fixed at setup (see §6.1) and does not change when a character dies: a dead character and a *lost* character still count.
new: The number of characters is the number taking part in the game (see §6.1). It does not change when a character dies: a dead character and a *lost* character still count. It changes only when a player joins or leaves the game (see §18.4).
rationale: A player may join or leave a standard game as well as a campaign (§18.4), so the count is not fixed at setup.

old: The number of characters in a campaign changes only when a player joins or leaves it (see §18.4).
rationale: Now stated once, for both kinds of game (lead-E05).

old: which is awarded when the encounter is *cleared* in the same way as a chest's treasure card (see §7.7).
new: which is awarded when the encounter is *cleared* in the same way as a chest's treasure card (see §7.7). In campaign play a Level 4 encounter is rewarded as the other encounters of its section are (see §18.1).
rationale: Points to the campaign rule made by campaign-E16.

old: **Treasure card.** Any card from a treasure deck: *starting equipment*, *class-specific treasure*, *common treasure*, *legendary treasure*, or *boss treasure*.
new: **Treasure card.** Any card from a treasure deck or from Blacksmith Andre's shop: *starting equipment*, *class-specific treasure*, *common treasure*, *legendary treasure*, *boss treasure*, or an *ember card* (see §4.4).
rationale: §4.4 and the glossary count an ember card as a treasure card; §2.5 did not.

old: - A sold boss treasure card is returned to the game box.
new: - A sold boss treasure card is returned to the game box, and so is any other sold card that came from no treasure deck: an *invader*'s treasure card or a Titanite Scale card.
rationale: A card that came from outside the decks no longer enters a treasure deck when it is sold, from which it could have been dealt as an ordinary reward.

old: 7. If the party consists of one character, place six *souls* on that character's dashboard (see §7.6).
new: 7. If the party consists of one character, place six *souls* on that character's dashboard (see §7.6). Before leaving the bonfire tile for the first time, that character may visit the *Firekeeper* and Blacksmith Andre as during a rest (see §11.3; §11.4).
rationale: The six souls exist to help a lone character through the first encounters, and could not be spent before a rest that costs a spark.
evidence: core memo, observation without an edit

old:
**Q.** Which weapon slot is the left weapon slot, and which is the right?

**A.** The left weapon slot is the weapon slot on the left of the dashboard as its player reads it, and the right weapon slot is the one on the right. A character moves cards between them only by the Equip minor action during an encounter (see §3.2; §10.1).
rationale: After the parry ruling (combat-E22) no rule depends on which weapon slot is which, so the question is withdrawn.

old: **Q.** Who holds the aggro token when its holder dies?
new:
**Q.** May the party return to the bonfire tile without resting?

**A.** No. The party returns to the bonfire tile only to rest (see §11.1).

**Q.** Who holds the aggro token when its holder dies?
rationale: States the consequence of core-E36 where players will look for it.
